speaker: Marcus Delano Webb
cascadeSummary: Submitted the Month-five disbursement batch for 7 households, bringing total disbursements to 52. All documentation is audit-ready. Reset outreach targeting based on updated neighborhood need patterns identified in Fruitvale, while maintaining West Oakland pipeline integrity.

statements.decision: Approved 7 additional households for disbursement with full compliance documentation
statements.quote: Fifty-two families now stabilized with relocation assistance—that's eighteen point five percent of target served with zero compliance exceptions.
statements.fullStatement: The West Oakland Stabilization Fund has completed review and authorization for seven additional households in the Month-five disbursement batch, bringing the total number of families served to fifty-two. All case files contain complete eligibility documentation and expenditure verification as required by the CDBG-derived compliance framework I implemented. Outreach targeting has been adjusted per emerging patterns showing comparable need in Fruitvale, while maintaining the West Oakland applicant pipeline. The authorization packet is en route to the Mayor's office with copies to Council Finance Committee.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C103: Month-five batch (7 HH) approved; total disbursed 52/280. Outreach reset per Fruitvale signal.

statements.decision: Maintained Saturday outreach at Adeline Street office
statements.quote: Every applicant who walks through our door gets two things: the truth about the timeline, and the certainty that their case won't get lost.
statements.fullStatement: The Adeline Street sub-office maintained its Saturday outreach schedule this cycle, processing eighteen new applications and providing status updates to forty-three existing applicants. While disbursement timing remains subject to executive authorization, our commitment to transparency and case integrity continues—each file moves through review, approval, and documentation phases with the same care I learned processing CDBG files at HUD. The upbeat neighborhood mood noted in this cycle's briefing reflects both the progress made and the work ahead.
